steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: What's goin' on with these soldiers?

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: They go down without puttin' up a proper fight, and they don't even react to us yellin'.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: They're already dead. They've been dead for... over 48 hours.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Chenchen, I know you're a copper, you're not mistaken when you see things, but these people were clearly standin' before we knocked them down, right?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: I saw a kind of Arts, among Reunion's ranks, that could control other people.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: But this and that don't resemble each other. If Amiya... if Rhodes Island's Cautus was here, she might be able to feel out the difference better than me.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: That kind of Arts refuted emotion and thought. It took living Sarkaz warriors and wore them down into walking weapons.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: But these Dublinn soldiers are dead without a doubt... There's just some intense emotion that's still burning in them, even after they've died.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Burning?

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: It's just a feeling.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: If this Arts had a definite form, if I used my Chi Xiao to cut through it, I'd imagine I'd be cutting through a fireball.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Wait, I've seen...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Purple flames.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Strange purple flames, burnin' in the eyes of dead soldiers...

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I saw the Arts you're describin', back in County Hillock.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I haven't seen it since... not once, all this time! Chenchen, we're almost there, aren't we? That Caster leadin' the spectre force in County Hillock, she's got to be somewhere around here!

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: I'll never forget how she looked... I'm dead sure I'll recognize her if I see her again, and when I do, I can find out the truth about Dublinn.

steps.name: Ch'en
steps.text: Right.

steps.name: Bagpipe
steps.text: Come on, then! We need to keep askin' around! Villagers, maybe caravans who've passed by... We'll find them, even if they're not the spectres for real!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Phew.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Patrol came brutally fast. It's lucky we've got good eyes on us.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Hah, you think those Victorian eejits say hello before they come snatching?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You lot move ahead, I'll take a proper count. Been worried we left somebody behind in all that panic just now...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Oh, that's right! Where's the doctor? Did nobody fetch her?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Didn't she say she was off by herself this morning? I'm not minding her business.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Besides, it's not going to be an issue if a Viccy soldier nabs her, right? She's not wanted.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Look, she is! We got her involved in all this last night!

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: It was dark out and the soldiers probably didn't catch her face properly, but how many Vouivre have you ever seen around here?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Well, if you can't help her, what's the point dossing about fretting the whole day?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Wait. Hold on, Caireann's here... Selmon, you did that on purpose.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You lied to her saying we'd lost track of a friend, and could she go looking...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Why? She was kind enough to save us, and share us some medicine... And you just left her for the army lot to snap up?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: You don't get it? We leave her behind to attract attention, and that gives us a safe getaway for the time being.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: And she won't say much vital even if she's caught. She doesn't even know which way we're going, let alone the fact we're looking for Dublinn.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: But... But she could die!

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: Yeah. She went off alone. She'll run into the patrol sooner or later.

steps.name: Taran Refugee
steps.text: We should've taken all her luggage while we had the chance. Wouldn't fall into those Victorian scumbags' hands, at least.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: It was her choice, Fionn. Did you not see her face when she saw me?

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: She KNEW Dublinn, but never had no kindness for it. And she spoke standard Victorian.

steps.name: Selmon
steps.text: Her sort hate us more than real Victorians do.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I can't swallow that, Selmon. I trust my intuition for people.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Relax, madam.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'm not—familiar with what's gone on here.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: I know. You're not a Dublinn ally. You just panicked for a bit, and got mixed up with those insurrectionists.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: (Taran) You've killed Dublinns.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: You understood that. We're not mistaken, then. There's very few Vouivre around these parts who know Taran.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Where did that Dublinn soldier take you lot, last night?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No... they're not Dublinn, and they don't have anything to do with Dublinn either.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: And I've never killed anyone from Dublinn before. You've gotten something wrong.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: You can be honest here. You won't pay for it, so you don't need to fear it.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: The land around here has been under strict surveillance by the barracks. The Marquess of Trent has no plans to dither like some nobility has, letting Dublinn stir up flames all over the place.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: That's why we could even tell who you were.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Residents of a different village, close to Trent's cityway, reported news of Dublinn to the barracks a few days ago.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: But those Dublinn soldiers, before they could attack the village, were all felled by a white-haired Vouivre.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Would we be able to turn on the tap, so to speak? We'd like to query your identity, motive, as well as last night's arson which held similarities to Dublinn MO...

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: —Hold it! Are you trying to flee?

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Stop her! This Vouivre is scared of going on record! There's something afoot with her!

steps.name: Patrol Soldier
steps.text: —S-She broke my saber?! What kind of strength does she...?!

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I've told you—everything I can tell you. Let me leave...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It'll be best for us.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: You must be of a kind with those wretches, if you're so protective of them. Bumptious Tara rabble, the lot of you.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Fire! A few bolts aren't enough to kill a Vouivre! Suppress her first!

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Why... do you hate them so much? You're a—Taran yourself...

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Shut up! You are NOT—to address me with that word!

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: So anyone who spoke Taran since childhood IS a Taran? I certainly never heard of the 'Taran' people when I was young!

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: If you're the one who repelled those Dublinns, you should get it into your head that 'Taran' is just an excuse of a moniker these bandits use to destroy the order. And once you do, you draw a clean line between yourself and them.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: ...'It was the erosion of the Tarans by Victoria's vain stylings, that led so many to fall to banditry.'

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: A mentor... told me this, many years ago.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'm sorry.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Hah, hah... you're hesitating. You're scared of even stabbing people with your pike there.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: —Are you looking down on me, is that it?
It was because, in an instant, they'd become ash upon the barrens.

steps.name: 'The Leader'
steps.text: Go, Loughshinny. If you don't want what you do to be discovered, then the best way is to dispose of all eyewitnesses.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: No, I wouldn't do that.

steps.name: Patrol Captain
steps.text: Urgh—!

steps.name: Patrol Soldier
steps.text: Captain!

steps.name: Patrol Soldier
steps.text: Re... Retreat with the captain! Report this upstairs, request backup!

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: It's okay. They won't—catch up to me.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I'll be leaving this place very soon. I know the speed—at which the Victorian Army mobilizes.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: This is—far from wrong to do.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: —Who's there?
She thrusts her spear forth in vigilance.
—Its point hovers over some shrubbery.

steps.name: Voice Behind a Shrub
steps.text: It's me, it's me...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: It's me, I'm not going to hurt you.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Yes, I'm very well aware the County Trent won't be changing its entire course just for a single order, which is why we're willing to push back the delivery date and wait for the nomadic city to come closer.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Of course, only mines with royal approval could provide Originium fuel of such high purity, hence my being so very thankful for the Marquess of Trent's friendly attitude to us.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: I imagine we're all very happy with this business partnership.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Your secretary has left with the signed contract, Mr. Hughes.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: He'll deliver it back to the office. Please, I ask you trust him to properly handle such a vital agreement.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: No, no no no, I don't mean to doubt his management abilities.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: But rather, doesn't this imply you have more pressing matters to discuss with me personally than the contract, mmm?

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: After all, you did choose this secluded little getaway, and dismiss your servants too.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: Quite right, it's no surprise you'd surmise, haha. I had all these arrangements laid out specifically to convey my good faith to you. My wish is that...

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: our ensuing conversation will be founded on our mutual friendship from our time studying at the Royal Guard together, Lo—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Shh.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: How funny you should remember that name.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: Haha... well, you do know how famous she was at the ball.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Oh, my, does it not make sense that her type could topple over and not get up while dead drunk in some godforsaken place?

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: Yes, I trust the vast majority have forgotten all about her. Whether it was a true accident or some other party's orchestration, everyone knew not to stick their noses into it.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: I much thank you for so lavishly feigning surprise.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: My surprise happens to contain a kernel of sincerity.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Bringing up a name vanished from the school, a name with no record anywhere in Victoria of existing... You're practically bidding 'spectres' to come.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: Hm, you're not wrong.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: Then let me be bold. Why, may I ask, did you contact me of your own accord? I'm no more than a minor aristocrat making minor deals with all the mercantile breadth. I couldn't do anything about the info you've hinted at.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: Miss Informant, are you looking to circumvent your higher-ups to please your own swollen ambitions, or are you...

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: If you've made full sense of this conversation, it wouldn't do me any more favors playing the fool, would it.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: The gist of it is, I'm here specifically, given our previous time studying at the Royal Guard, to offer you... and the two who've been searching for the spectre force this whole time, a little warning.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: You knew...

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Mm, yes, of course I knew they came to see you, plus that you helped them pursue a batch of Originium products shipped to County Hillock half a year ago.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Some people would sayyyy... you've let slip a little too much.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: I understand how sensitive your position is, and how multifaceted your responsibilities. Rest assured, I would absolutely never leak any of this classified information to anyone.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: As for those two rash students of mine, I'll give them a tact warning to quit while they're ahead.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: And I'll leave your staff a little head start on their investigation into your order's whereabouts.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: I appreciate your kindness, but being the paltry merchant I am, I fear I shouldn't be privy to too much.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: No, please, drop the humbleness. After all, you're the vice-chair of your commerce coalition. I'd think the Earl that backs you would very much care about any info you gather doing business.

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: Is the Iron Duke really so worth depending on, given his sheer silence up to now? You know, it's about time he decided where he stood.

steps.name: Hughes
steps.text: Harmonie, you're not telling me you're Victoria's... no, just who are you serving—

steps.name: Harmonie
steps.text: —Mr. Hughes, I'd be very happy to receive the contents of our next contract from you... sooner, rather than later.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Sorry, sorry... Really, I'm not here to hurt you, please don't touch me.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* I couldn't will myself to come out just now, sorry I didn't help you...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: What am I on about? You're good enough with your spear there to knock a soldier out in a swing or two. Hardly needing anyone else to help you, haha.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You should have withdrawn by now.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: We... *sigh* Okay, you guessed as much.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: So, did they leave you behind too?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: They shouldn't... they wouldn't. You can't fight. You'd get caught.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: But you're a trader here—you know so many people. If they treat you unjustly, you have too many methods you could retaliate with...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: No, no. I was actually... running back to bring you along, so you can flee with us.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I know, I'm a little late for that. I was feeling guilty, and scared of running into the army, and I just kept arguing with myself, and now I'm late.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: It's a good thing you can fight, at least. The army can't get their hands on you.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Er, ma'am, sa... say something. You're frightening me, you really are.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: I am? ...Why?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I really don't know how to apologize to you in any way that makes it better. Honestly, they're a kind bunch usually, it's just life these days has driven us mad...

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You don't need to say anything... it's fine. I don't mind.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Think of me like... like reeds, growing on the roadside.
I won't poison you, or crush you. At most, you'll feel a little stinging from me.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Who would mind—such a white lie?

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: You say that with your hurt written all over your face.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: Do... I look that hurt?

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: You don't need... to worry about me, but—you do need to flee, quickly.

steps.name: Reed
steps.text: After last night's fire, the army will be sure to transfer more people from the city, to search the wilds here.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Er, right, of course...

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: *sigh* There's one more thing, actually. It's a little hard for me to say.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: I know you're telling us to run. But for the past dozen or so days, we've been hounded by the army this way and that like beasts in a hunting ground, just going in circles over the wastes. We can't shake them.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: So if I could ask you one more favor.

steps.name: Fionn
steps.text: Please, help us. Escort us on our journey, so we can catch the carrier truck that saves our lives.
